Engineering philosophy

I'm a software engineer with 6+ years of experience designing and shipping backend systems at companies where scale is a first-class constraint, not an afterthought.

My work lives in the space between a product requirement and a production incident — distributed systems, event-driven pipelines, platform infrastructure that other engineers depend on. I don't just write code that works; I write code that the next engineer can reason about at 2am when something goes wrong.

I care about the boring stuff: observability, runbooks, on-call hygiene, Architecture Decision Records. The work that doesn't ship a feature but determines whether the team can sleep.

Before writing a single line of code, I write the failure modes. I model systems as queues, caches, and consistency boundaries. I present trade-offs in writing before they become production incidents. I treat documentation as a first-class engineering deliverable.

Currently open to senior and staff engineering roles with a strong infrastructure, platform, or systems mandate.
